title: Time, days & months
goal: Tell and ask the time, name the days and months, and talk about today, tomorrow, last week and next month.
intro:
Time in Nepali is 'struck' like a bell: **कति बज्यो?** literally means 'how much has struck?'. You'll learn clock times, the parts of the day, the days of the week (they all end in **-बार**) and the twelve months of Nepal's own calendar, the Bikram Sambat.

Good to know: Nepal's clocks run at **UTC+5:45** — one of the few time zones in the world with a 45-minute offset.

vocab.en: to strike, ring (of clocks, bells, phones)
vocab.note: कति बज्यो? 'What time is it?'; तीन बजे 'at three o'clock'.

vocab.en: the day before yesterday; the other day

vocab.note: अब के गर्ने? 'What do we do now?'
दुई दिनपछि 'two days later', खानापछि 'after the meal'.
Also अघि aghi: तीन दिन अघि 'three days ago'.
Many offices close early on Friday.

phrases.en: What time do you get up?
I get up at six in the morning.
Until what time is the shop open?

phrases.native: बिहान दस बजेदेखि बेलुका सात बजेसम्म।
phrases.roman: bihāna das bajedekhi belukā sāt bajesamma.
phrases.en: From ten in the morning till seven in the evening.

phrases.note: गते gate = day of the Nepali month; for Western dates people say तारिख tārikh.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.body:
**कति बज्यो?** 'What time is it?' — answer with the hour + **बज्यो** 'has struck': तीन बज्यो 'it's three'.

**Quarters and halves** come before the hour:
सवा तीन 3:15 · साढे तीन 3:30 · पौने चार 3:45
Special: **डेढ** 1:30 and **अढाई** 2:30 (not साढे एक/दुई).

**Minutes**: तीन बजेर दस मिनेट गयो '3:10' (lit. having struck three, ten minutes went); चार बज्न दस मिनेट बाँकी छ '3:50' (lit. ten minutes remain for four to strike).

**At** a time: use **बजे** — तीन बजे 'at three'. Add the part of the day in front: बिहान सात बजे '7 a.m.', दिउँसो दुई बजे '2 p.m.', बेलुका छ बजे '6 p.m.', राति दस बजे '10 p.m.'.

examples.en: Let's have a snack at half past one.

examples.native: पाँच बज्न दस मिनेट बाँकी छ।
examples.roman: pāṃch bajna das mineṭ bāṃki chha.

grammar.title: Days, months and the Nepali calendar
grammar.body:
Days of the week all end in **-बार**. You don't need a word for 'on': सोमबार आउनुहोस् 'come on Monday'. **Saturday (शनिबार)** is the weekly day off; Sunday is a working day.

Nepal officially uses the **Bikram Sambat** (वि.सं.) calendar. The year begins in mid-April, and the months are:
**बैशाख** baisākh (Apr–May) · **जेठ** jeṭh · **असार** asār · **साउन** sāun · **भदौ** bhadau · **असोज** asoj · **कात्तिक** kāttik · **मंसिर** mansir · **पुस** pus · **माघ** māgh · **फागुन** phāgun · **चैत** chait (Mar–Apr).
A day of the month is **गते**: बैशाख एक गते = Nepali New Year's Day. Western dates (तारिख) and English month names are used too, especially in business.

examples.en: Dashain falls in (the month of) Asoj.

examples.native: नयाँ वर्ष बैशाख एक गते हो।
examples.roman: nayāṃ barsa baisākh ek gate ho.
examples.en: New Year is on the 1st of Baisakh.

grammar.title: Time expressions: ago, later, from…to
grammar.body:
• **-पछि** 'after/later': दुई दिनपछि 'in two days', कामपछि 'after work'.
• **अघि / पहिले** 'ago/before': तीन दिन अघि 'three days ago', खानाभन्दा पहिले 'before the meal'.
• **-देखि … -सम्म** 'from … until': सोमबारदेखि शुक्रबारसम्म 'Monday to Friday'. -देखि alone also means 'since': हिजोदेखि 'since yesterday'.
• **यो** 'this', **अर्को** 'next', **गएको / गत** 'last': यो हप्ता, अर्को महिना, गएको साल. 'Next' can also be **आउने** 'coming': आउने आइतबार 'next Sunday'.
• For a period, no word for 'for' is needed: दुई घण्टा पर्खेँ 'I waited (for) two hours'.

examples.en: I'll come back in two weeks.
The office is open from Monday to Friday.

dialogue.title: Let's meet on Friday
dialogue.setting: Bikash phones Sarah to make plans.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: ठीक छ। तपाईं भोलि बेलुका खाली हुनुहुन्छ?
lines.roman: ṭhik chha. tapāiṃ bholi belukā khāli hunuhunchha?
lines.en: All good. Are you free tomorrow evening?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: शुक्रबार म छ बजेसम्म अफिसमा हुन्छु।
lines.roman: sukrabār ma chha bajesamma aphismā hunchhu.
lines.en: On Friday I'm at the office until six.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: त्यसो भए साढे सात बजे भेटौँ?
lines.roman: tyaso bhae sāḍhe sāt baje bheṭauṃ?
lines.en: Then shall we meet at half past seven?

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: पाटन दरबार स्क्वायरको अगाडि। नेपाली टाइम होइन है!
lines.roman: Pāṭan Darbār Skwāyarko agāḍi. nepāli ṭāim hoina hai!
lines.en: In front of Patan Durbar Square. And not 'Nepali time', OK!

culture: Nepalis joke about **नेपाली टाइम** 'Nepali time' — a meeting at 'seven' may start at half past. Festivals follow the lunar calendar, so their dates move every year: **Dashain** usually falls in Asoj or Kattik (Sept–Oct), **Tihar** a few weeks later, and the New Year **(नयाँ वर्ष)** on 1 Baisakh in mid-April. Official documents, school years and birthdays are usually given in Bikram Sambat (वि.सं. २०८३ ≈ 2026–27 AD), so if a Nepali friend says they were born in 2055, they mean about 1998!

tip.title: Telling the time
tip.body:
- **कति बज्यो?** 'What time is it?' Answer: hour + **बज्यो**: तीन बज्यो 'it's three'.
- Quarters and halves go *before* the hour: **सवा** तीन 3:15, **साढे** तीन 3:30, **पौने** चार 3:45.
- But 1:30 is **डेढ** and 2:30 is **अढाई**.

sentences.en: Is it half past two already?
What time is it by your watch?

tip.title: 'At six': बजे
tip.body:
- 'At' a time is **बजे**: छ **बजे** 'at six'. (बज्यो is only for 'it is…'.)
- Put the part of the day in front: **बिहान** सात बजे 7 a.m., **दिउँसो** दुई बजे 2 p.m., **बेलुका** छ बजे 6 p.m., **राति** दस बजे 10 p.m.
- How long: दुई **घण्टा**, दस **मिनेट** (no word for 'for').
tip.pattern: बिहान / दिउँसो / बेलुका / राति + hour + बजे

sentences.native: म बिहान साढे छ बजे उठ्छु।
sentences.roman: ma bihāna sāḍhe chha baje uṭhchhu.
sentences.en: I get up at half past six in the morning.
Let's eat at two in the afternoon.
Come to the house at six in the evening.
I go to bed at ten at night.
What time do you get up? (to a friend)
What time does the bus leave?
I'm at home in the afternoon.

tip.title: Time words first
tip.body:
- Time words usually come first and need no 'on': **भोलि** भेटौँ 'let's meet tomorrow'.
- **हिजो** 'yesterday' and **अस्ति** 'the other day' go with past verbs (गयो, आएँ); **भोलि** and **पर्सि** with present/future ones (जान्छु).
- **अहिले** = 'at the moment'; **अब** = 'now, from now on, next'.

sentences.en: The day after tomorrow I'm going to Patan.
I went to Thamel the other day.

tip.title: Days end in -बार
tip.body:
- Every day ends in **-बार**: आइतबार, सोमबार, मङ्गलबार, बुधबार, बिहीबार, शुक्रबार, शनिबार.
- No word for 'on': **सोमबार** आउनुहोस् 'come on Monday'.
- **शनिबार** (Saturday) is the day off; Sunday is a working day.
- 'What day?' = के बार? 'What date?' = कति गते? (Nepali calendar).

sentences.en: Are you free on Friday evening?
Come on Monday at ten in the morning.

lessons.title: From when till when?

tip.title: Before, after, from … until
tip.body:
- **-पछि** 'after / in': दुई दिन**पछि** 'in two days', खाना**पछि** 'after the meal'.
- **अघि** 'ago', **पहिले** 'before, first': दुई महिना **अघि** 'two months ago'.
- **-देखि … -सम्म** 'from … until': सोमबार**देखि** शुक्रबार**सम्म**.
- यो हप्ता 'this week', अर्को महिना 'next month'.
tip.pattern: X-देखि Y-सम्म  ·  दुई दिनपछि  ·  दुई दिन अघि

new: बिहान दस बजेदेखि बेलुका सात बजेसम्म।

sentences.en: The shop opens from eight in the morning.
I'm at the office Monday to Friday.
Let's have tea after the meal.

sentences.native: म दुई महिना अघि नेपाल आएँ।
sentences.roman: ma dui mahinā aghi Nepāl āeṃ.
sentences.en: I came to Nepal two months ago.
Let's have tea first, then eat.
Until what time is the office open?
I don't have time this week.
Next month I'm going to India.
